facts: Safia Abukar Farole authored the paper published on April 1, 2023 in Comparative Politics.
The paper examines how ethnic parties historically dominated by one group diversify their representatives under local electoral institutions in South Africa.
South Africa uses a Mixed-Member Proportional (MMP) electoral system where parties nominate both Single Member District (SMD) and Proportional Representation (PR) candidates.
The empirical analysis relies on original data on the racial, ethnic, and career background of over 10,000 local candidates nominated by the historically white Democratic Alliance (DA) party.
The study finds that the DA engages in vote-based inclusion by nominating black candidates to predominantly black districts.
The DA practices symbolic inclusion on its PR lists, where non-whites are included but white candidates dominate electable list positions.
The findings provide a micro-level demonstration of why ethnic parties struggle to achieve meaningful diversification.
